function: Downlink sum-rate beamforming in cell-free massive MIMO: DNNs give initial beamforming and parameters (weights, powers, update ratios) of a decentralized WMMSE algorithm (p. 1, p. 6-7).
system: Cell-free massive MIMO downlink: M=32 APs with N=4 antennas serve K=4 single-antenna UEs; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, p. 10).
method: Model-based DL: fully connected DNNs (4 hidden layers, 200 nodes) inside decentralized WMMSE; unsupervised sum-rate loss, offline training plus distributed online fine-tuning (p. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: APs and UEs uniform in 300 m circle, path-loss exponent 3, Rayleigh fading; Rician and CDL-A/B/C/D (TR 38.901) only for adaptation tests (p. 9-10, p. 14-15).
test_conditions: Offline: Rayleigh fading, M=32 APs (M=40 for Fig. 4); tested on 24-64 APs without retraining; adapted online to Rician, 20 dB SNR, CDL-B/C/A after CDL-D (p. 10-11, 14-15).
baselines: Non-learned: centralized C-WMMSE, decentralized D-WMMSE, LRZF initial beamforming; learned: conventional NC of [17], fully connected DNNs with DNN-oriented fronthaul messages (p. 10).
metrics: Average sum-rate versus fronthaul coordinations, number of APs, orthogonal resources (fronthaul overhead), SNR, K, N; CPU run-time; number of trainable parameters (p. 10-14).
complexity: Asymptotic order O(Lglobal(NK^2+C_DNNs)), C_DNNs = DNN forward-pass costs, versus C-WMMSE O(Lglobal*M(NK^2+Llocal*K*N^3)) (p. 9); CPU run-time 0.169 s versus 8.341 s, M=32, N=4, K=4 (p. 13).
openness: none (no code or data link in the paper).
q1_support: p. 15: "using a Clustered Delay Line (CDL) channel model dataset, in which each scenario has different channel distributions with predetermined path angles and delays as specified in [46]" (ref. [46] is 3GPP TR 38.901, p. 16: "document TR 38.901, 3GPP"); only this adaptation experiment uses CDL, the rest uses a custom simulator.
q2_support: p. 11: "trained with M = 40 dataset and then evaluated in M ∈ {24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64} environments without additional training" (also p. 15: trained offline on CDL-D, then applied to CDL-B, CDL-C and CDL-A).
q3_support: p. 10: "C-WMMSE [25]: This scheme provides a sub-optimal solution utilizing global CSI" (non-learned) and "Conventional NC [17]: This approach relies on DNNoriented uplink and downlink messages" (earlier learned fully connected design); both compared on sum-rate (Figs. 3-8, 10).
q4_support: p. 9: "The computational complexity of the proposed NC framework, which has the L-D-WMMSE-based decentralized inference, is stated as" an O(.) expression; p. 13: "Table II lists the average CPU run-time [sec] of one fronthaul coordination".
q5_support: p. 10: "The training and test dataset is randomly generated with the considered channel statistics"; no link or DOI to code or data anywhere in the paper, and no public dataset is used.
notes: Included, area 3 (beamforming): DNN components inside a decentralized WMMSE produce the AP precoders. q1 rests only on the CDL-D to CDL-B/C/A adaptation experiment (Fig. 12, p. 15; TR 38.901 is ref. [46], p. 16), while the other results use a custom Rayleigh/Rician simulator, so the reviewer should confirm. The learned baseline conventional NC follows ref. [17] and is re-implemented by the authors with parameter sharing and non-orthogonal coordination (p. 10). Table II was read from the page image (p. 13). No frequency band is given.
